citation: A committee of five representing the Association of Teachers of Psychology in Iowa. (1911). Preparation for Examinations in Psychology. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/edu
title: Recommended list of ten psychology textbooks with Elementary and Advanced requirements
description: To secure a uniform basis for the examinations, the committee recommends ten texts, including Betts, Angell, Kirkpatrick, James, Seashore, Judd, Dewey, Titchener, Calkins, and Thorndike, each annotated (e.g., Seashore's is "A manual of experiments not requiring any laboratory"). The article states "In the Elementary examination, three of these are required; in the Advanced, six." Special books are Kirkpatrick, Seashore, and Dewey; the others are general introductions. A supplementary reference list for public libraries is also given.
requirements: Candidates select two general and one special text for the Elementary examination, four general and two special for the Advanced
constraints: The state examination will be based specifically upon the recommended books only until January 1, 1915, with a revision published January 1, 1914
target_learners: Teachers seeking Elementary or Advanced psychology certification in Iowa
target_learning_goals: Preparation for uniform state psychology examinations
key_sources: A committee of five representing the Association of Teachers of Psychology in Iowa. (1911). Preparation for Examinations in Psychology. The Journal of Educational Psychology. https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/edu

citation: Vania Dimitrova. (2003). STyLE-OLM: Interactive Open Learner Modelling. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://telearn.hal.science/hal-00197312
title: Adaptive learning systems should diagnose learners through interactive open learner modelling
description: Because diagnosing a learner's cognitive capacity is crucial for adaptive systems, the article recommends conceiving diagnosis as an interactive process: systems should let the learner discuss and jointly construct the learner model. The authors argue IOLM "is a fruitful approach which may be employed in intelligent learning environments".
requirements: An intelligent learning environment that opens the learner model to inspection and negotiation with the learner
target_learners: learners using adaptive computer-based learning systems
target_learning_goals: improved diagnosis of the learner's cognitive state
examples: STyLE-OLM implements this approach by having the system and learner discuss and together construct the learner model
key_sources: Vania Dimitrova. (2003). STyLE-OLM: Interactive Open Learner Modelling. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://telearn.hal.science/hal-00197312

article_title: Characterizing academic performance in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia with population-based achievement tests.
citation: Al‐Kaylani HM, Reasoner EE, Loeffler BT, Mott SL, Madasu S, Liu A, Langbehn K, Conrad AL, Dickens D, Grafft A, Harshman L, Modi AJ, van der Plas E. (2022). Characterizing academic performance in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia with population‐based achievement tests. Cancer Reports. https://doi.org/10.1002/cnr2.1560
title: Iowa Assessments obtained in a school setting as an ecologically valid measure of academic performance
description: The Iowa Assessments are validated, annually administered achievement tests measuring reading, math, and science in Iowa public and private schools. The article uses school-administered Iowa Assessment scores precisely because psychological achievement tests lack ecological validity: "these measures are typically administered in a quiet testing space with a dedicated examiner. By contrast, most school activities occur while experiencing significant environmental distractions." The tests show composite reliability coefficients of 0.927–0.983 and strong associations with ACT scores.
requirements: Partnership with an educational agency (the Iowa Department of Education) to obtain statewide test scores and program-participation data
constraints: Per the authors' agreement with the Iowa Department of Education, state means could not be specified on plots
examples: The study collected 269 observations across grades 3–11 from 63 ALL survivors treated between 2000 and 2019 at the University of Iowa
key_sources: Al‐Kaylani HM, Reasoner EE, Loeffler BT, Mott SL, Madasu S, Liu A, Langbehn K, Conrad AL, Dickens D, Grafft A, Harshman L, Modi AJ, van der Plas E. (2022). Characterizing academic performance in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia with population‐based achievement tests. Cancer Reports. https://doi.org/10.1002/cnr2.1560

article_title: Framework for interprofessional case conferences - empirically sound and competence-oriented communication concept for interprofessional teaching.
citation: Posenau André, Handgraaf Marietta. (2021). Framework for interprofessional case conferences – empirically sound and competence-oriented communication concept for interprofessional teaching. GMS Journal for Medical Education. https://www.egms.de/en/journals/zma/2021-38/zma001461.shtml
title: Use a competence-oriented performance examination (iOSCE) driven by the framework rather than outcome-only assessment
description: Because "assessment drives learning", the article argues a competence-oriented examination is needed at module end. The framework makes the process observable and evaluable with an empirical basis instead of evaluator introspection, since each discussed aspect "can be captured empirically". Basing evaluation exclusively on case-conference outcomes is judged unsatisfactory; performance in interprofessional interaction is the most relevant criterion.
requirements: An examination format that captures the process aspects empirically
constraints: Until now teaching concentrated on cases at the expense of communication development
examples: In the 7th semester an interprofessional objective structured clinical examination (iOSCE) is used as the graded module exam
key_sources: Posenau André, Handgraaf Marietta. (2021). Framework for interprofessional case conferences – empirically sound and competence-oriented communication concept for interprofessional teaching. GMS Journal for Medical Education. https://www.egms.de/en/journals/zma/2021-38/zma001461.shtml
